questions.explanation: Xylem is a vascular tissue that conducts water and dissolved mineral ions mainly from roots to aerial parts and also provides mechanical support; most conducting elements are dead at maturity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is phloem?

options.A: A vascular tissue that conducts water and minerals
options.B: A vascular tissue that transports sugars and other organic substances from sources to sinks
options.C: A tissue that covers the outer surface of the plant
options.D: A supporting tissue with thick lignified walls

questions.explanation: Phloem is a vascular tissue that transports sugars and other organic substances from sources to sinks; sieve elements are living but lack a nucleus at maturity in angiosperms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is translocation in plants?

options.A: Movement of water through xylem
options.B: Movement of organic solutes, especially sucrose, through phloem from source regions to sink regions
options.C: Loss of water vapour from leaves

questions.explanation: Translocation in plants is the movement of organic solutes, especially sucrose, through phloem from source regions to sink regions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the essential macronutrients for plants?

options.A: Iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine and nickel
options.B: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur

questions.explanation: The essential macronutrients for plants are carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur; macronutrients are required in relatively large amounts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are essential micronutrients for plants?

options.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium
options.B: Iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine and nickel

questions.explanation: Essential micronutrients for plants are iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine and nickel; they are required in small amounts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nitrogen used for in plants?

options.A: It is a component of amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids and chlorophyll-related metabolism
options.B: It regulates stomatal function
options.C: It is part of ATP and phospholipids

questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a component of amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids and chlorophyll-related metabolism; deficiency often causes yellowing of older leaves.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the role of phosphorus in plants?

options.A: It is part of ATP, nucleic acids and phospholipids and supports energy transfer, root development and reproduction
options.B: It regulates enzyme activity and osmotic balance
options.C: It is a component of chlorophyll

questions.explanation: Phosphorus is part of ATP, nucleic acids and phospholipids and supports energy transfer, root development and reproduction.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the role of potassium in plants?

options.A: It is part of ATP and nucleic acids
options.B: It regulates enzyme activity, osmotic balance, stomatal function and stress responses
options.C: It is a component of chlorophyll

questions.explanation: Potassium regulates enzyme activity, osmotic balance, stomatal function and stress responses.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are auxins?

options.A: Plant hormones involved in cell elongation, apical dominance, root initiation, tropic responses and fruit development
options.B: Plant hormones that promote stem elongation and seed germination
options.C: Plant hormones that promote cell division
options.D: A gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening

questions.explanation: Auxins are plant hormones involved in cell elongation, apical dominance, root initiation, tropic responses and fruit development.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are gibberellins?

options.A: Plant hormones involved in cell elongation and apical dominance
options.B: Plant hormones that promote stem elongation, seed germination, flowering in some species and fruit growth
options.C: Plant hormones that promote cell division and delay leaf senescence
options.D: A gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening

questions.explanation: Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation, seed germination, flowering in some species and fruit growth.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are cytokinins?

options.A: Plant hormones that promote cell division and can delay leaf senescence
options.B: Plant hormones that promote stem elongation
options.C: Plant hormones involved in apical dominance
options.D: A gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening

questions.explanation: Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division and can delay leaf senescence; they interact with auxins in organ development.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is ethylene?

options.A: A plant hormone involved in cell elongation
options.B: A gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening, leaf abscission, senescence and stress responses
options.C: A plant hormone that promotes cell division
options.D: A plant hormone that promotes seed germination

questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening, leaf abscission, senescence and stress responses.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is abscisic acid (ABA)?

options.A: A plant hormone important in stress responses, seed dormancy and closure of stomata during water stress
options.B: A plant hormone that promotes stem elongation
options.C: A gaseous plant hormone involved in fruit ripening
options.D: A plant hormone that promotes cell division

questions.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a plant hormone important in stress responses, seed dormancy and closure of stomata during water stress.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is pollination?

options.A: The fusion of male and female gametes
options.B: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma in flowering plants

questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma in flowering plants; it may be self-pollination or cross-pollination.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is fertilisation in flowering plants?

options.A: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
options.B: Fusion of a male gamete with the egg cell to form a zygote
options.C: The formation of the seed coat

questions.explanation: Fertilisation in flowering plants is the fusion of a male gamete with the egg cell to form a zygote; angiosperms also undergo double fertilisation, producing the endosperm through fusion of another sperm with the polar nuclei/central cell.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is double fertilisation?

options.A: Fusion of two sperm with the egg cell
options.B: A characteristic of angiosperms in which one sperm fuses with the egg to form the zygote and another fuses with the central cell nuclei to form endosperm
options.C: Fertilisation occurring twice in a lifetime
options.D: Fertilisation of two eggs by one sperm

questions.explanation: Double fertilisation is a characteristic of angiosperms in which one sperm fuses with the egg to form the zygote and another fuses with the central cell nuclei to form endosperm.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is germination?

options.A: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
options.B: Resumption of embryo growth in a viable seed under suitable conditions

questions.explanation: Germination is the resumption of embryo growth in a viable seed under suitable conditions, commonly requiring water, oxygen and an appropriate temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is vegetative propagation?

options.A: Sexual reproduction in plants
options.B: Asexual reproduction in plants from vegetative parts such as stems, roots or leaves
options.C: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
options.D: The formation of seeds after fertilisation

questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction in plants from vegetative parts such as stems, roots or leaves; examples include potato tubers, onion bulbs, runners and cuttings.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are microorganisms?

options.A: Organisms too small to be seen clearly without magnification
options.B: Only bacteria

questions.explanation: Microorganisms are organisms or biological agents too small to be seen clearly without magnification; groups include bacteria, microscopic fungi, protozoa and microscopic algae, while viruses are acellular agents.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are bacteria?

options.A: Single-celled eukaryotic organisms
options.B: Single-celled prokaryotic organisms lacking a membrane-bound nucleus

questions.explanation: Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotic organisms lacking a membrane-bound nucleus; they show diverse shapes and metabolisms and may be beneficial, harmless or pathogenic.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are common bacterial shapes?

options.A: Cocci, bacilli, spirilla and vibrios
options.B: Round, square, triangular and oval

questions.explanation: Common bacterial shapes include cocci (spherical), bacilli (rod-shaped), spirilla/spirochaetes (spiral) and vibrios (comma-shaped).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are viruses?

options.A: Single-celled prokaryotic organisms
options.B: Acellular infectious agents consisting of genetic material enclosed in a protein capsid, sometimes with a lipid envelope; they replicate only inside host cells

questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular infectious agents consisting of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein capsid, sometimes with a lipid envelope; they replicate only inside host cells.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Are antibiotics effective against viruses?

options.A: Yes, all antibiotics work against viruses
options.B: No. Antibiotics target bacterial structures or processes and do not treat viral infections
options.D: Yes, if given in high doses

questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial structures or processes and do not treat viral infections.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are fungi?

options.A: Prokaryotic organisms lacking a nucleus
options.B: Eukaryotic organisms that absorb nutrients; many have chitin-containing cell walls and reproduce by spores
options.D: Photosynthetic organisms with cellulose cell walls

questions.explanation: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that absorb nutrients; many have chitin-containing cell walls and reproduce by spores. Yeasts are unicellular fungi and moulds are generally filamentous.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are protozoa?

options.A: A traditional grouping of mostly unicellular eukaryotic organisms, many of which are motile and feed on organic matter
options.B: Multicellular animals

questions.explanation: Protozoa are a traditional grouping of mostly unicellular eukaryotic organisms, many of which are motile and feed on organic matter; some cause disease.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which microorganism is commonly used in bread-making?

options.A: Lactobacillus
options.B: Yeast, especially Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Yeast, especially Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is commonly used in bread-making; it ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide that makes dough rise.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which bacteria are commonly involved in curd formation?

options.A: Yeast species
options.B: Lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus species, which convert lactose into lactic acid

questions.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus species and related genera convert lactose into lactic acid, causing milk proteins to coagulate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is biological nitrogen fixation?

options.A: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or related usable forms by certain microorganisms
options.B: Conversion of ammonia into nitrogen gas

questions.explanation: Biological nitrogen fixation is the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or related usable forms by certain microorganisms, including Rhizobium in legume root nodules and some free-living bacteria and cyanobacteria.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who discovered penicillin?

options.A: Louis Pasteur
options.B: Alexander Fleming

questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming observed penicillin's antibacterial effect in 1928; Howard Florey, Ernst Boris Chain and colleagues later developed it for medical use.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is pasteurisation?

options.A: Controlled heating of food or liquids, followed by cooling, to reduce pathogenic microorganisms and spoilage organisms
options.B: The complete sterilization of food
options.D: The addition of preservatives to food

questions.explanation: Pasteurisation is controlled heating of food or liquids, followed by cooling, to reduce pathogenic microorganisms and spoilage organisms; it does not make every product sterile.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a pathogen?

options.A: A beneficial microorganism
options.B: A microorganism or infectious agent capable of causing disease in a host

questions.explanation: A pathogen is a microorganism or infectious agent capable of causing disease in a host.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Porifera?

options.A: Sponges; mostly marine, pore-bearing animals with a canal system, no true organs and specialised collar cells called choanocytes
options.B: Aquatic animals with radial symmetry and stinging cells
options.D: Segmented worms with a true coelom

questions.explanation: Porifera are sponges; they are mostly marine, pore-bearing animals with a canal system, no true organs and specialised collar cells called choanocytes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Cnidaria (Coelenterata)?

options.A: Sponges with choanocytes
options.B: Aquatic animals with radial symmetry, a gastrovascular cavity and stinging cells called cnidocytes

questions.explanation: Cnidaria are aquatic animals with radial symmetry, a gastrovascular cavity and stinging cells called cnidocytes; examples include Hydra, jellyfish and corals.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Platyhelminthes?

options.A: Sponges with a canal system
options.B: Flatworms with bilateral symmetry, three germ layers and no true body cavity
options.D: Segmented worms with a true coelom

questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes are flatworms with bilateral symmetry, three germ layers and no true body cavity; many are parasitic, such as tapeworms and liver flukes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Nematoda?

options.A: Flatworms without a body cavity
options.B: Roundworms with an unsegmented cylindrical body, a pseudocoelom and a complete digestive tract
options.C: Segmented worms with a true coelom
options.D: Molluscs with a mantle and muscular foot

questions.explanation: Nematoda are roundworms with an unsegmented cylindrical body, a pseudocoelom and a complete digestive tract; examples include Ascaris and hookworms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Annelida?

options.A: Segmented worms with a true coelom and organ-system level organisation
options.B: Roundworms with a pseudocoelom
options.D: Animals with jointed appendages and exoskeletons

questions.explanation: Annelida are segmented worms with a true coelom and organ-system level organisation; examples include earthworms, leeches and many marine worms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Arthropoda?

options.A: Segmented worms with a true coelom
options.B: Jointed appendages, segmented body and a chitinous exoskeleton; the largest animal phylum
options.C: Soft-bodied animals with a mantle and muscular foot
options.D: Marine animals with a water vascular system

questions.explanation: Arthropoda have jointed appendages, a segmented body and a chitinous exoskeleton; it is the largest animal phylum and includes insects, arachnids, crustaceans and myriapods.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Mollusca?

options.A: Jointed appendages and exoskeleton
options.B: Soft-bodied animals, usually with a muscular foot, visceral mass and mantle; many have a shell
options.C: Segmented worms with a true coelom
options.D: Marine animals with a water vascular system

questions.explanation: Mollusca are soft-bodied animals, usually with a muscular foot, visceral mass and mantle; many have a shell. Examples include snails, clams and octopuses.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Echinodermata?

options.A: Jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton
options.B: Exclusively marine animals with a water vascular system and tube feet; adults commonly show five-part radial symmetry
options.D: Segmented worms with a true coelom

questions.explanation: Echinodermata are exclusively marine animals with a water vascular system and tube feet; adults commonly show five-part radial symmetry, while larvae are bilateral.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Amphibia?

options.A: Ectothermic vertebrates with moist skin; many have aquatic larvae and undergo metamorphosis
options.B: Ectothermic vertebrates with dry, keratinised scales
options.D: Vertebrates with hair and mammary glands

questions.explanation: Amphibia are ectothermic vertebrates with moist skin; many have aquatic larvae and undergo metamorphosis, while adults may live on land and in water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Reptilia?

options.A: Ectothermic vertebrates with moist skin
options.B: Ectothermic vertebrates with dry, keratinised scales or scutes and lungs; most lay amniotic eggs
options.D: Vertebrates with hair and mammary glands

questions.explanation: Reptilia are ectothermic vertebrates with dry, keratinised scales or scutes and lungs; most lay amniotic eggs, though some give birth to live young.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Aves?

options.A: Ectothermic vertebrates with scales
options.B: Feathered, endothermic vertebrates with beaks, wings, lungs and air sacs; most lay hard-shelled eggs
options.C: Vertebrates with hair and mammary glands

questions.explanation: Aves (birds) are feathered, endothermic vertebrates with beaks, wings, lungs and air sacs; most lay hard-shelled eggs.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of Mammalia?

options.A: Ectothermic vertebrates with scales
options.B: Hair or fur, mammary glands that produce milk, three middle-ear bones and a single dentary bone in the lower jaw

questions.explanation: Mammals have hair or fur, mammary glands that produce milk, three middle-ear bones and a single dentary bone in the lower jaw; most give birth to live young, with monotremes as an exception.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between ectothermic and endothermic animals?

options.A: Ectotherms generate substantial metabolic heat; endotherms rely mainly on external heat sources
options.B: Ectotherms rely mainly on external heat sources to regulate body temperature; endotherms generate substantial metabolic heat and regulate internal temperature
options.C: Ectotherms are always cold; endotherms are always hot

questions.explanation: Ectotherms rely mainly on external heat sources to regulate body temperature; endotherms generate substantial metabolic heat and regulate internal temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which insect produces commercial silk?

options.A: Honeybee
options.B: The domesticated silkworm, Bombyx mori

questions.explanation: The domesticated silkworm, Bombyx mori, whose larva spins a silk cocoon, produces commercial silk.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which insect produces lac?

options.A: Bombyx mori
options.B: Apis species

questions.explanation: Lac insects, especially Kerria lacca (formerly Laccifer lacca), secrete resinous lac used to make shellac and other products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the role of honeybees?

options.A: They produce silk
options.B: They produce honey and beeswax and are important pollinators of many crops and wild plants

questions.explanation: Honeybees produce honey and beeswax and are important pollinators of many crops and wild plants.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a parasite?

options.A: An organism that lives in or on a host and obtains resources at the host's expense
options.B: An organism that produces its own food

questions.explanation: A parasite is an organism that lives in or on a host and obtains resources at the host's expense, usually causing some degree of harm.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an intermediate host?

options.A: A host in which a parasite reaches sexual maturity
options.B: A host in which a parasite undergoes essential developmental stages but does not usually reach sexual maturity
options.C: The primary host of a parasite
options.D: A host that is not affected by the parasite

questions.explanation: An intermediate host is a host in which a parasite undergoes essential developmental stages but does not usually reach sexual maturity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a definitive host?

options.A: A host in which a parasite undergoes essential developmental stages but does not reach sexual maturity
options.B: A host in which a parasite reaches sexual maturity or undergoes sexual reproduction
options.C: A host that is not affected by the parasite
options.D: A host that transmits the parasite to humans

questions.explanation: A definitive host is a host in which a parasite reaches sexual maturity or undergoes sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an example of a human parasite and its disease?

options.A: Plasmodium species cause malaria and use humans and female Anopheles mosquitoes as hosts at different stages of their life cycle
options.B: Escherichia coli causes malaria

questions.explanation: Plasmodium species cause malaria and use humans and female Anopheles mosquitoes as hosts at different stages of their life cycle.
